Context/Background:
Cancer-induced systemic inflammation is a dominant feature of cancer progression and metastatic spread. Clinically, systemic accumulation of myeloid cells is strongly correlated to poor prognosis in multiple solid malignancies, including breast cancer and a high neutrophil-to-lymphocyte (NLR) ratio is consistently associated with adverse outcomes. We, and others, previously published that primary tumors induce systemic accumulation and activation of neutrophils leading to enhanced metastatic spread in preclinical mouse models. In steady state, hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) give rise to all circulating blood cells through a series of progressively restrictive differentiation steps regulated by coordinated and temporal expression of transcription factors (TFs), leading to balanced bone marrow (BM) output. However, the molecular processes driving chronic, cancer-induced hematopoiesis, which leads to systemic inflammation, remain poorly understood.

We have previously demonstrated that expansion of metastasis-supporting neutrophils in mammary tumor-bearing K14cre;Cdh1fl/fl;Trp53fl/fl (KEP) mice is driven by an inflammatory cascade in which tumor associated macrophage (TAM)-derived IL-1β leads to elevated serum levels of G-CSF, the principal instructor of neutrophil generation. To understand how and at what stage of differentiation tumors drive neutrophil expansion, we clustered the genes upregulated in tumor-bearing mice based on their dynamics along the neutrophil pseudotime trajectory. We identified three groups of differentially expressed genes in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from KEP mice, which we termed early, middle, and late, based on their expression patterns. 

Early genes showed significant enrichment of an HSC-specific gene set. Upregulated early genes were overexpressed in HSCs and multipotent progenitors (MPPs) from KEP mice compared to cells from control mice but were repressed in cells that were further along the inferred neutrophil differentiation trajectory. Middle genes were defined as genes that were expressed around the transition from MPP to granulocyte monocyte progenitor (GMP). Lastly, upregulated/downregulated late genes, expressed in late GMP, granulocyte progenitor (GP), and pro-neutrophil (ProNeu) populations, were found to be expressed prematurely and at a higher level in progenitors from KEP mice.
Prompt: Provide a summary of the relevant pathways and genes that are up and down regulated in KEP vs WT mice in early, intermediate and late neutrophil development, focusing on how and at what stage of differentiation tumors drive neutrophil expansion.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
KEP mice (K14cre;Cdh1^fl/fl;Trp53^fl/fl mammary tumor model) exhibit systemic neutrophil expansion driven by a TAM-derived IL-1β→G-CSF axis. Single-cell RNA-seq of BM hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from tumor-bearing (KEP) versus wild-type (WT) mice was ordered along a neutrophil pseudotime trajectory and genes up-regulated in KEP HSPCs clustered into Early (HSC/MPP), Intermediate (MPP→GMP transition), and Late (late GMP/GP/ProNeu) groups. The provided Table S1 lists gene_symbol and cluster membership (Up/Down × Early/Intermediate/Late) but contains no fold-changes or p-values (not specified). We performed ORA on each gene‐cluster set across MSigDB_Hallmark, KEGG_2021_Human, KEGG_2016, and GO_Biological_Process_2023 libraries to identify pathways enriched at each differentiation stage.

Keywords  
• Neutrophil differentiation  
• IL-1β / JAK-STAT signaling  
• HSC / progenitor  
• Inflammatory response  
• G-CSF axis  

Candidate Genes  
STAT3, SOCS3, IL1R1, CEBPA, MYD88  

Pathway Enrichments  

Early stage (HSC/MPP; Up Early vs Down Early)  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP):  
• Interferon Gamma Response | Direction: Up Early | Leading Genes: IFITM3, LGALS3BP, RTP4, CD274, P2RY14, STAT3, EIF2AK2, IFI44, ISG15, ICAM1, SELP, SOCS3, PLSCR1, RNF213, SOCS1, OAS3, CASP4, TNFSF10, PIM1, PDE4B, IRF7  
• IL-6/JAK/STAT3 Signaling | Direction: Up Early | Leading Genes: SOCS3, JUN, SOCS1, IL1R1, STAT3, PIM1, MAP3K8, DNTT, IL2RG, ACVR1B, PIK3R5  

KEGG_2021_Human (UP):  
• Axon guidance | Up Early | CAMK2D, SEMA4D, SEMA3D, CAMK2A, PIK3CD, PRKCA, RHOD, ABLIM1, RGS3, PPP3CC, PLCG2, EPHB2, SRGAP1, NEO1  
• Acute myeloid leukemia | Up Early | ITGAM, STAT3, PIM1, RARA, PIK3CD, PIM2, PPARD  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP):  
• Negative Regulation Of Receptor Signaling Pathway Via STAT | Up Early | SOCS3, GBP7, SOCS1, BCL3  
• Cellular Response To Interleukin-2 | Up Early | STAT3, IL2RG, JAK3  

KEGG_2016 (UP):  
• cGMP-PKG signaling pathway | Up Early | TRPC6, PPP1R12A, INSR, GNAQ, AKT3, ATP2A3, ATP2B4, PDE5A, MEF2D, PIK3CG, PRKG1  
• Acute myeloid leukemia | Up Early | TCF7L2, CCND1, AKT3, KIT, PIK3CG  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN):  
• UV Response Down | Down Early | SMAD3, ZMIZ1, AKT3, MAGI2, KIT, ATP2B4, PTPRM, ADGRL2, IGF1R  
• Interferon Gamma Response | Down Early | CD74, AUTS2, IL15, STAT4, PDE4B, NLRC5, TXNIP, IRF9  

KEGG_2021_Human (DOWN):  
• cGMP-PKG signaling pathway | Down Early | PPP1R12A, TRPC6, INSR, GNAQ, AKT3, ATP2A3, ATP2B4, PDE5A, MEF2D, PIK3CG, PRKG1  
• UV Response Down | Down Early | SMAD3, ZMIZ1, AKT3, MAGI2, KIT, ATP2B4, PTPRM, ADGRL2, IGF1R  

Analysis  
At the earliest HSC/MPP stage, KEP-up genes are dominated by interferon and JAK–STAT inflammatory programs (STAT3, SOCS3, IL1R1) reflecting an IL-1β→G-CSF–driven inflammatory cascade. By contrast, Down Early genes show repression of stress-response modules (UV Response Dn) and select interferon signatures. In the Intermediate phase (MPP→GMP), ORA highlights metabolic reprogramming (Cysteine/methionine metabolism) and Myc/ cell-cycle checkpoints in Up Intermediate, whereas Down Intermediate engages angiogenesis and apoptotic pathways. Late progenitors (Late Up) load onto mTORC1 signaling, unfolded protein/ER stress, and p53-linked apoptosis, with MYD88 emerging in Toll-like receptor/inflammatory routes. Down Late clusters lose granulocytic regulators such as CEBPA and engage p53/ rejection modules, suggesting premature lineage exit.

Targeted subset (IL-1β / JAK-STAT-related terms in Up Early ORA)  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: IL-6/JAK/STAT3 Signaling (Adjusted p = 5.9×10^–8)  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: Cellular Response To Interleukin-2 (Adjusted p = 5.1×10^–3)  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading-edge)  
Up direction:  
| Gene   | Direction  | Role/Function                                 | Pathway(s)                     |  
|--------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|  
| STAT3  | Up Early  | Cytokine-activated TF mediating G-CSF/IL-6    | IL-6/JAK/STAT3, IFNγ Response  |  
| SOCS3  | Up Early  | Feedback inhibitor of JAK–STAT signaling      | IL-6/JAK/STAT3, IL-2/STAT5     |  
| IL1R1  | Up Early  | IL-1 receptor mediating TAM-derived signal    | Inflammatory Response          |  
| MYD88  | Up Late   | Adapter for IL-1R/TLR signaling               | TLR/Inflammatory Response      |  

Down direction:  
| Gene   | Direction  | Role/Function                                 | Pathway(s)                     |  
|--------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|  
| CEBPA  | Down Late | TF controlling granulocyte differentiation    | p53 Pathway, Allograft Rejection|  

Comparisons  
Early enrichment of cytokine/STAT programs concords with known IL-1β→G-CSF–mediated neutrophil induction, whereas intermediate stages shift to metabolic and proliferative modules, and late stages engage stress/apoptosis pathways, reflecting accelerated but dysregulated maturation. The suppression of CEBPA at Late may underlie aberrant progenitor expansion.

Implications  
Targeting STAT3/SOCS3 feedback loops could normalize early neutrophil progenitor skewing. Inhibitors of metabolic node PHGDH or mTORC1 may block intermediate expansion. Modulating ER stress or p53 signaling at late stages could restore balanced differentiation and limit metastasis-supportive neutrophil maturation.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate STAT3 phosphorylation dynamics in KEP versus WT HSPCs along pseudotime.  
2. Assess functional consequences of CEBPA repression on progenitor colony-forming assays.  
3. Profile G-CSF receptor (Csf3r) expression along the trajectory (not observed in cluster membership).  
4. Clarify whether replication/cell-cycle (E2F, G2/M) and mitochondrial/stress pathways (ER stress) are sequentially induced by tumor-derived cytokines.
